predecessors.note: Split from the same Cliopatria row; Norway went to Sweden. Greenland, Iceland and the Faroe Islands were 'Excepted' from the cession.

land.text: the Danish state after the German surrender; 'On 5 May 1945, Denmark was officially free of German control'

successors.note: The Danish state continued under German occupation from 9 April 1940 and was free of German control on 5 May 1945; Cliopatria's modern Denmark row starts in 1945 (fx-46 R139: this dossier now runs to May 1945 and hands the land to denmark). Nazi Germany is not a successor: it occupied, it did not annex ('the government remained functioning de jure until the end of the war').

correction.text: Denmark, Schleswig, Holstein, Iceland and the Faroes without Swedish Pomerania, which was promised at Kiel but never handed over

keyframe_review.note: 1814: 185,172 km2: Denmark, Schleswig, Holstein, Iceland, the Faroes and 14 cells of Swedish Pomerania (Mecklenburg-Vorpommern). Article VII of the Treaty of Kiel provided that Swedish Pomerania 'was to be handed over to Denmark', but the page has 'Charles XIII released his Pomeranian subjects on 1 October 1815' and the province 'handed over to Prussian officials' on 23 October 1815, after Denmark and Sweden gave up their claims at Vienna: Denmark never held it. The correction removes those cells (17 with a Syddanmark cell of Cliopatria's jitter). Greenland is not in the shape (no cell west of Iceland).

1815-1847: 181,517 km2 (Iceland alone is 103,000 km2 on the Denmark-Norway page). +7 cells for Lauenburg: 'This duchy was then handed over from Prussia to Denmark, along with an additional payment of 3.5 million thalers' (1815). Stable for 33 years.

Holds 1848-1850. Out: Schleswig, Holstein and Lauenburg (87 cells, 160,660 km2 left), exactly Cliopatria's Duchy of Holstein shape: 'In March 1848, the Low German-speaking population of Schleswig, Holstein, and Lauenburg rebelled' and 'created a provisional government and army'. The page's war runs 24 March 1848 to 8 May 1852; the rebel army was disbanded on 1 April 1851, so the Danish shape returns in 1851, not 1853 (next keyframe).

correction.text: Denmark with Schleswig, Holstein and Lauenburg again under the Danish crown

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1851-1852: 'On 1 April 1851, the Schleswig-Holstein army was disbanded'; the infobox gives 'Status quo ante bellum' and the final settlement is the London Protocol of 8 May 1852. Cliopatria returns the land in 1853.
1853-1863: the 1815 shape again (181,517 km2); Cliopatria's restoration is two years after the page's end of the rebel army and one after the London Protocol.

Holds 1864-1917; 160,323 km2 after Schleswig, Holstein and Lauenburg go: 88 cells, 32% of the 275 non-Iceland cells of the 1853 shape, against the page's 'the land area of the Danish monarchy decreased by 40%' (population 2.6 to 1.6 million): the same order (the page does not say whether Iceland is counted). Iceland is wrong from 1918 and the shape lacks North Schleswig from 1920; two new keyframes follow.

correction.text: the 1864 shape without Iceland, a sovereign kingdom in personal union from 1 December 1918

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1918-1919: 'On 1 December 1918, the Act of Union, an agreement with Denmark, recognized Iceland as a fully sovereign state', 'an independent country in personal union with Denmark through a common monarch'. A personal union is not territory (rule 4), so Iceland (458 cells) leaves the shape in 1918, four years before Cliopatria drops it; Cliopatria's Kingdom of Iceland row starts in 1918.

correction.text: Denmark without Iceland, with North Schleswig regained in 1920, and the Faroes

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1920-1921: 'In 1920 the country regained possession of the northern part of Schleswig' (20 cells that Cliopatria adds in 1922). The Denmark page dates the reunification 10 July 1920.
1922-1935: 202 cells, 53,400 km2: Denmark with North Schleswig and the Faroes, without Iceland. Dated two years after the reunification of 1920 (the page gives the year only).

1940: 4 cells, 1,430 km2: the Faroe Islands only, which British forces occupied from 12 April 1940 ('a pre-emptive bloodless invasion'). Denmark proper is in Cliopatria's Nazi Germany shape (197 of 202 cells) after 'German forces crossed the border into neutral Denmark' at 4:15 on 9 April 1940, so the year is drawn as the end of the state; January to 8 April 1940 was the full 1936 shape (month resolution only). Adjusted by fx-46 R139: Cliopatria's 4-cell row is the Faroes only, but the Danish state did not end in 1940 ('the government remained functioning de jure until the end of the war'; the King stayed), so the 1936 shape is carried through 1945 and the German occupation is hatched over it (this dossier's ledger 12-13, occupation_start/end with counterpart nazi-germany).

correction.text: Denmark proper and the Faroe Islands as in 1936: the Danish state, king and de jure government, stayed under German occupation from 9 April 1940 to 5 May 1945

region.text: the Danish kingdom after the Treaty of Kiel: Denmark, Schleswig and Holstein, with Iceland and the Faroe Islands

ledger.note: 14 January 1814: the Treaty of Kiel leaves the Danish crown without Norway. Denmark 'irrevocably and forever' renounced claims to the Kingdom of Norway (Article IV); Greenland, Iceland and the Faroe Islands were 'Excepted' and stayed Danish. The treaty also promised Swedish Pomerania to Denmark, never carried out (keyframe 1814).

1815: Denmark receives Lauenburg at the Congress of Vienna. Denmark and Sweden gave up Swedish Pomerania in favour of Prussia and 'This duchy was then handed over from Prussia to Denmark, along with an additional payment of 3.5 million thalers.' The page gives no month for the handover of Lauenburg.

region.text: Schleswig and Holstein with Lauenburg, 87 cells, the territory of the rebel provisional government (Cliopatria's Duchy of Holstein 1848-1852)

ledger.note: March 1848: Schleswig, Holstein and Lauenburg rebel. 'In March 1848, the Low German-speaking population of Schleswig, Holstein, and Lauenburg rebelled' and 'created a provisional government and army'; 'The German Confederate Diet recognizes the provisional government of Schleswig' on 12 April and Prussian troops cross the Dannevirke on 19 April 1848. Counterpart: Cliopatria's Duchy of Holstein row, whose 1848 shape is these 87 cells.

region.text: Schleswig and Holstein with Lauenburg, 87 cells, the territory of the rebel provisional government (Cliopatria's Duchy of Holstein 1848-1852)

ledger.note: 1 April 1851: the rebellion ends. 'On 1 April 1851, the Schleswig-Holstein army was disbanded'; the infobox gives 'Status quo ante bellum' (24 March 1848 to 8 May 1852) and the Danish victory at Idstedt, 24-25 July 1850, preceded it. The London Protocol of 8 May 1852 was 'the final settlement of the conflict with the great powers'. Cliopatria returns the land in 1853.

1 February 1864: Prussia and Austria invade. 'The war began on 1 February 1864, when Prussian and Austrian forces crossed the border into the Danish fief Schleswig.' Counterpart is the row that carries Prussia in 1864: Cliopatria's Kingdom of Prussia row ends in 1863, and Austria is in the loss event.

region.text: all of Jutland, the Danish mainland

ledger.note: 14 July 1864: Jutland falls. 'The Prussian general Eduard Vogel von Falckenstein signs his name in the church book at Skagen. With this, all of Jutland, the Danish mainland, is occupied by the Germans.'
30 October 1864: the Treaty of Vienna. 'The war ended on 30 October 1864, with the Treaty of Vienna and Denmark's cession of the Duchies of Schleswig'.

region.text: all of Jutland, the Danish mainland

ledger.note: 30 October 1864: Jutland stays Danish; the page says 'Denmark kept the island of Ærø and some other areas' and does not date the end of the occupation of Jutland, so the treaty date is used.

intersect.text: the Duchies of Schleswig, Holstein and Lauenburg

region.text: Schleswig and the northern part of the ceded duchies, as Cliopatria gives them to the German Confederation

ledger.note: 30 October 1864: 'Denmark ceded Schleswig, Holstein and Lauenburg to Prussia and Austria.' Infobox: 'Denmark loses Schleswig, Holstein and Lauenburg'. Cliopatria shares the 88 cells between its German Confederation row (51, Schleswig and north Holstein), its Austrian Empire row (34) and neither (3); Prussia and Austria administered Schleswig and Holstein from the Gastein Convention of 14 August 1865.

intersect.text: the Duchies of Schleswig, Holstein and Lauenburg

region.text: the ceded duchies as Cliopatria gives them to the Austrian Empire

ledger.note: 30 October 1864: the Austrian share of the same cession (34 cells at 53.6-54.4 N).

1 December 1918: Iceland becomes a sovereign kingdom. 'On 1 December 1918, the Act of Union, an agreement with Denmark, recognized Iceland as a fully sovereign state', 'an independent country in personal union with Denmark through a common monarch'. Cliopatria keeps Iceland in the Danish shape to 1921.

region.text: the northern part of Schleswig (North Schleswig), 20 cells

ledger.note: 10 July 1920: North Schleswig returns to Denmark. 'On 10 July 1920, Northern Schleswig was recovered by Denmark' (Denmark page; month added by the eu-14-g reviewer); the German occupation of Denmark page has 'In 1920 the country regained possession of the northern part of Schleswig', lost in the Second Schleswig War in 1864.

region.text: Denmark proper (Jutland, the islands and Bornholm), without the Faroes

ledger.note: 9 April 1940: 'On 9 April 1940, Germany invaded Denmark in Operation Weserubung'; the King 'remained in the country as Danish head of state' and 'the government remained functioning de jure until the end of the war'. Recorded by the owner with the roles reversed (Germany occupies, this state keeps the land) so the hatch is drawn: nazi-germany ledger 13 names the counterpart 'denmark', which is not alive before May 1945 and holds no cells, so that record hatches nothing while this state holds Denmark. Added by the fx-46 review (R139).

region.text: Denmark proper (Jutland, the islands and Bornholm), without the Faroes

ledger.note: 5 May 1945: the occupation 'lasted until the Allied victory on 5 May 1945'; 'On 5 May 1945, Denmark was officially free of German control'. Closes the occupation of 1940 (fx-46 review, R139).

region.text: Denmark proper and the Faroe Islands: the Danish state as it stood in 1936 and, under occupation, to 1945

ledger.note: 5 May 1945: 'On 5 May 1945, Denmark was officially free of German control'; the occupation that began on 9 April 1940 'lasted until the Allied victory on 5 May 1945'. The state did not end in 1940: King Christian X stayed as head of state, and after the King never accepted the cabinet's resignation 'the government remained functioning de jure until the end of the war' (Germany took direct military control after 29 August 1943; the Folketing did not convene). The occupation is booked here from the owner's side (ledger 12-13, occupation_start / occupation_end with counterpart nazi-germany), so this state keeps its land, hatched; nazi-germany ledger 13 and 79 name 'denmark' (alive only from May 1945) and hatch nothing. Was a dissolve into nazi-germany in April 1940 (fx-46 R139). The new denmark dossier is founded in May 1945 with this one as predecessor. Not drawn: British forces from 12 April 1940 on the Faroe Islands (no end date on the page); Bornholm under Soviet forces until April 1946.

wars.name: First Schleswig War

zones.text: Schleswig and Holstein with Lauenburg, 87 cells, the territory of the rebel provisional government (Cliopatria's Duchy of Holstein 1848-1852)

wars.outcome: Danish victory, 'Status quo ante bellum': Prussia made peace with Denmark at Berlin on 2 July 1850, the Danes won at Idstedt on 24-25 July 1850, the rebel army was disbanded on 1 April 1851 and the London Protocol of 8 May 1852 closed the settlement.

zones.text: the Duchies of Schleswig, Holstein and Lauenburg
all of Jutland, the Danish mainland

wars.outcome: Austro-Prussian victory: the Treaty of Vienna of 30 October 1864 gave Schleswig, Holstein and Lauenburg to Prussia and Austria; the Danish monarchy lost 40% of its land area; Denmark kept Ærø and some other areas.
wars.note: Began 1 February 1864; ceasefire of 12 May 1864 broke down; Als fell on 29 June; all Jutland occupied by 14 July.

wars.name: German invasion of Denmark (9 April 1940)

zones.text: Denmark proper, occupied by German forces

wars.outcome: German occupation of Denmark from 9 April 1940 to 5 May 1945, without annexation; British forces occupied the Faroe Islands from 12 April 1940.
wars.note: The page is the occupation article; the invasion of one day is its first sentence.

certainty.note: Treaty lines: the Eider frontier of Schleswig and Holstein to 1864, the treaty line of 1864 and the 1920 plebiscite line; the 1848-1850 front in Schleswig between the rebels and the Danes is not a line.

Occupied by Germany from 9 April 1940; the state and its frontier are carried as in 1936. The Faroes (British forces from 12 April 1940) and Bornholm (Soviet forces to 1946) are not drawn as occupied.

notes: Written by the Phase B agent for batch eu-14-g, 2026-10-25. SPLIT: the second half of Cliopatria's 'Denmark-Norway' row (1526-1940, 30 shapes): the shapes of 1814-1940 (8) are reviewed here, those of 1526-1809 are in denmark-norway (same batch). Shape ids keep the Cliopatria slug (denmark-norway_1814 ...); the 3 new keyframes carry this slug. The row is the Danish kingdom after the Treaty of Kiel; new slug because the union ended in 1814. COVERS: Denmark with Schleswig and Holstein (Lauenburg from 1815), Iceland and the Faroes; Greenland is in none of this row's shapes; Cliopatria draws the colony as its own row, Greenland (1734-1940) (see denmark-norway notes); the Danish West Indies, Danish India and the Gold Coast are separate Cliopatria rows. WHERE CLIOPATRIA IS WRONG HERE: (1) Swedish Pomerania is drawn Danish in 1814 although it never was (keyframe 1814). (2) Iceland stays in the shape to 1921 although it was sovereign from 1 December 1918 (new keyframes 1918, 1920). (3) The Danish shape returns after the rebellion in 1853, the page has 1 April 1851. (4) The row ends in 1940 with only the Faroes: Denmark proper is inside Cliopatria's Nazi Germany shape in 1940-1944 and its Denmark row starts in 1945; the Danish state continued under occupation until 5 May 1945, which a gap-filler may want to draw as a hatched occupation of Denmark from 1940 to 1945 (the pages opened say the government 'remained functioning de jure'). COUNTERPARTS: the rebels of 1848-1851 are Cliopatria's duchy-of-holstein (eu-20); the 1864 cession is split between german-confederation (51 cells, standing in for Prussia, whose row ends in 1863) and austrian-empire (34 cells). UNVERIFIED: the shape sizes for 1815-1847 and 1853-1863 have no infobox area on the pages opened (the Danish monarchy's 40% loss of 1864 is the only area check); the 1807-1809 detail is in denmark-norway. PAGES: 6 (Treaty of Kiel, First and Second Schleswig War, Kingdom of Iceland, German occupation of Denmark, List of Danish monarchs) against a budget of 5 for 8 shapes, one over; the Kiel page and the monarch list are shared with denmark-norway, which used 10 more pages for 22 shapes (budget 9). FX-46 R139 (3 Nov 2026): the dossier now runs to 5 May 1945 (identity.end 1945/5, dissolve into denmark, keyframe 1940 widened to the 1936 shape through 1945, nazi-germany no longer a successor); the slug keeps '1814-1940' only because slugs are fixed. Before, the land was nobody's from the 1940 dissolve (a plain 'occupied nobody' by p1940-p1949 events/9-10, which now find no free cells).
